title: Slow Cooker Turkey, Potato & Corn Chowder
description: Deli or cooked turkey, potatoes, corn, and milk make a gentle, familiar crockpot chowder with no specialty ingredients.

ingredients.item: russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
chopped cooked turkey or deli turkey

substitutions: Use cooked chicken instead of turkey.
Use canned corn, drained, instead of frozen corn.
Leave out the cheddar for a lighter chowder.

steps.text: Mash a little, then add turkey and milk.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds diced potatoes, 2 cups chicken broth, 2 cups frozen corn, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder in the slow cooker. Cover and cook on LOW 4 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes right in the cooker with a potato masher or fork so the broth becomes creamy while plenty of potato pieces remain.
Stir in 2 cups chopped cooked turkey and 1 cup milk. Cover and cook on HIGH 15 minutes, until steaming hot.
Stir in 1/2 cup shredded cheddar if using. Taste, season with salt and pepper as needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days, counting from when the turkey was originally cooked. Reheat gently until steaming hot; add a splash of milk if thick.

title: Sheet-Pan Ham, Broccoli & Cheddar Potatoes
description: Crisp-edged potatoes, broccoli, ham, and melted cheddar make an easy sheet-pan dinner from everyday ingredients.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of ham.
Use cauliflower florets instead of broccoli.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 1/2 pounds diced potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using. Spread on a large sheet pan and roast 18 minutes.
Toss 2 cups broccoli florets with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Add the broccoli and 2 cups diced cooked ham to the pan, stir everything, and roast 10 minutes more.
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded cheddar over the pan and return it to the oven for 2 minutes, just until melted.
Serve hot. Add salt and pepper to taste.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in the microwave until steaming hot.

title: Leftover Chili & Cheddar Rice Bowls
description: Leftover chili stretches into a fast rice bowl with corn and cheddar for a filling 10-minute lunch or dinner.
substitutions: Use cooked quinoa or small pasta instead of rice.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Skip the corn or use frozen peas.

cookSteps.text: Put 2 cups leftover chili and 1/2 cup corn in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir 5–6 minutes until bubbling and steaming hot. If using a microwave, cover loosely and heat in short intervals, stirring between them.
Warm 2 cups cooked rice until steaming hot.
Divide the hot rice between 2 bowls. Spoon the chili mixture over it and top with 1/2 cup shredded cheddar.
Add 1 tablespoon sour cream or plain yogurt to each bowl if using and serve.

storage: Use only while the original chili and rice are still within their safe refrigerated storage windows. Refrigerate assembled leftovers up to 1 day and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter & Jam Oat Bars
description: A small pan of soft peanut-butter oat bars gets a familiar jam swirl for an inexpensive pantry sweet.
equipment: small loaf pan or 6-inch baking dish
substitutions: Use any flavor of jam you like.
Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
For a less sweet bar, reduce brown sugar to 3 tablespoons.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a small loaf pan or 6-inch baking dish.
Mix 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar, and 1 egg until smooth. Stir in 3/4 cup oats and 1/4 cup flour until evenly combined.
Press the mixture into the prepared pan. Drop 1/4 cup jam over the top in small spoonfuls and gently swirl it through the surface with a butter knife.
Bake 18–20 minutes, until the edges are set and the center no longer looks wet.
Cool at least 15 minutes before cutting into 6 bars.

storage: Store covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days.
